name: Mathematical Foundations
crownClaim: Mathematical reasoning provides a consistent, formal framework for deriving necessary truths from axioms, applicable to modeling physical reality
instructions: Research each claim. Some are axiomatic. Cross-chain dependencies on epistemic_foundations noted. Focus evidence on foundational mathematics papers, Goedel's theorems, and the applicability of mathematics to physics.

claims.claim: The natural numbers can be axiomatized (Peano axioms) providing a consistent foundation for arithmetic
ZFC set theory provides a consistent axiomatic foundation for most of mathematics
A formal proof guarantees truth-preservation from axioms to theorems within the system
Any consistent formal system powerful enough to encode arithmetic is incomplete — there exist true statements it cannot prove (Goedel)
Mathematics can model physical systems with predictive accuracy far exceeding chance
Mathematical reasoning provides a consistent formal framework for deriving necessary truths, applicable to modeling physical reality

alternatives.claim: Mathematics is purely formal symbol manipulation with no necessary connection to physical reality
Classical logic (law of excluded middle) should be rejected; only constructive proofs are valid
